The case of the prosecution is that Firstly, on or before 22.07.1999 all the accused entered into a criminal conspiracy and in pursuance of the said conspiracy, all the accused cheated DDA by violating existing rules and regulations and extending illegal assistance to accused Shashi Bhushan in order to get a cheque of Rs. 1,21,266/- issued from DDA in the name of original allottee Abhishek Soni and getting the same encashed in the account of Shashi Bhushan by filling up wrong particulars in the deposit slip, pay in slip and withdrawal slip therefore causing wrongful loss to DDA and wrongful gain to themselves and thereby all the accused committed offence u/s 420/120B of IPC.

Secondly, on or before 22.07.1999 all the accused in pursuance of the said conspiracy cheated DDA and filled wrong particulars in the deposit slip, pay in slip and withdrawal slip and encashed a sum of Rs. 1,21,266/- and thereby committed offence u/s 419/120B of IPC.
Thirdly, on or before 22.07.1999 all the accused in pursuance of the said conspiracy forged certain documents as mentioned in the charge-sheet purported to be a valuable security and got a cheque for Rs. 1,21,266/- issued from DDA in the name of Abhishek Soni and by misusing the bank account in FIR No. 483/2000 State Vs. Jai Prakash Ors. 2 of 8 BHANU by BHANU PRATAP SINGH PRATAP

Fourthly, on or before 22.07.1999 all the accused in pursuance of the said conspiracy forged certain documents as mentioned in the charge-sheet intending that it shall be used for the purpose of cheating and thereby committed offence u/s 468/120B of IPC.

Fifthly, on or before 22.07.1999 all the accused fraudulently and dishonestly used as genuine the above-said forged documents mentioned in the charge-sheet which the accused knew or had reason to believe to be forged and thereby committed offence u/s 471/120B of IPC.

As per the charge-sheet, accused no. 1 Jai Prakash Gupta, accused no. 2 Dinesh Manocha,
accused no. 5 Jai Prakash Sharma and accused no. 6 S.C. Chugh were DDA officials.
Accused no. 3 is Shashi Bhushan.
The proceedings against accused no. 4 Om Prakash Arora were abated on 06.02.2010 as he had expired.
REASONS FOR DECISION 03.
The whole case of the prosecution is based on alleged violation of rules and regulations of DDA including violation of the policy dated 31.03.1999 of DDA by the accused persons.

As per the prosecution witnesses PW-4 VD Arora and PW17 Sanjeev Kumar, the accused persons working in DDA deliberately violated the rules and regulations of DDA including DDA policy dated 31.03.1999 in order to process the refund in the name of allottee Abhishek Soni and the processing of refund was done on forged application in the name of allottee Abhishesk Soni which was submitted to DDA in public hearing.
FIR No. 483/2000 State Vs. Jai Prakash Ors. 3 of 8 BHANU by BHANU PRATAP SINGH PRATAP

The defence of the accused persons namely accused no. 1 Jai Prakash Gupta, accused no. 2 Dinesh Manocha, accused no. 5 Jai Prakash Sharma and accused no. 6 S.C. Chugh who were DDA officials is that they did not violate the DDA policy dated 31.03.1999 by processing the refund in the name of allottee Abhishek Soni.
The accused persons further took the defence that there was no conspiracy between the accused persons to forge any valuable security and no forgery as alleged was done by the accused persons.
05. PW4 V.D. Arora stated in his cross-examination dated 15.03.2016 that 'I cannot say whether Abhishek Soni was entitled for refund or not.
Again said : Abhishek Soni was not entitled for any refund from DDA'' .
06. PW4 V.D. Arora in his cross-examination dated 15.03.2016 stated that it is correct that the possession of the flat was not handed over to Abhishek Soni in time as per the SFS Scheme.

PW4 further stated that Abhishek Soni was not entitled for payment of belated construction interest as the allocation of the flat stood cancelled because he did not deposit the demanded amount on time.
PW4 further stated that the cancellation of the allotment of Abhishek Soni was subsequently restored by the competent authority.

PW4 further stated that it is specifically mentioned in the policy dated 31.03.1999 that in all such cases that have been restored by the competent authority,
belated construction interest would be paid.
07. On perusal of the testimony of PW4 it is evident that PW4 has given contrary versions on whether allottee Abhishek Soni was entitled to refund as per policy dated 31.03.1999.

This Court is of the view that difference in interpretation of DDA policy dated 31.03.99 and any decision taken by the FIR No. 483/2000 State Vs. Jai Prakash Ors. 4 of 8 BHANU Digitally by BHANU signed State vs Jai Parkash Ors on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199295568/

pursuant to such interpretation by itself does not constitute Criminal conspiracy.
The prosecution has to establish by evidence that there was a meeting of mind between accused persons to commit an illegal act.
The opinion of the PW4 and PW 17 on the actions of the accused persons in view of the policy dated 31.03.99 does not qualify as evidence of meeting of mind to commit an illegal act.
08. Perusal of testimony of PW6 Abhishek Soni shows that he admitted his signature on special power of attorney Ex.PW3/A.

Perusal of testimony of PW7 RK Goswami shows that he admitted his signature on special power attorney Ex.PW3/A.
09.
PW 17 in his cross examination dated 25.11.2024 stated that RK Goswami was the SPA holder of the allottee Abhishek Soni in this matter.
PW 17 further stated that RK Goswami appeared before the then Asstt. Director, DDA on 22.07.1999 and put his driving license as his identity proof while taking the possession of the flat in question.

10. Perusal of testimony of Abhishek Soni and RK Goswami shows that Both Abhishek Soni and RK Goswami did not state that they were forced by any of the accused to sign the special power attorney Ex.PW3/A or they were deceived by any of the accused to sign the special power of attorney.

Both Abhishek Soni and RK Goswami did not state that any of the accused forged stamps or seal of notary on the special power attorney Ex.PW3/A or on documents Ex.PW3/B, Ex.PW3/C, Ex.PW3/D and Ex.PW3/E.
Further perusal of testimony of PW17 shows that PW17 did not recover any forged stamps or seal of notary from the possession of any accused.

On perusal of the record and testimony of PW 17 Sanjeev Kumar, this Court is of the view that there is no evidence on record to show that accused DDA officials forged Special Power of Attorney Ex.PW3/A or documents Ex.PW3/B, Ex.PW3/C, Ex.PW3/D and Ex.PW3/E in order to process and approve the refund in the name of allottee Abhishek Soni.
Further there is no evidence on record to prove that the undated applications Ex.PW4/E and Ex.PW4/I in the name of Abhishek Soni were written or signed by accused persons.
Further no evidence has been brought on record that shows that accused had knowledge that the above stated applications were not prepared and signed by Abhishek Soni.
12. The prosecution has relied on the testimony of PW15 Tika Ram to prove criminal conspiracy between the accused persons.
Perusal of testimony of PW15 shows that PW15 himself signed the documents Ex.PW15/A, Ex.PW15/B, Ex.PW15/E and Ex.PW4/K.
PW15 in his entire testimony has not stated that he was forced to sign these documents or he was deceived to sign these documents by the accused persons.
Further as per the testimony of PW15, he is not aware of the policy dated 31.03.1999.

Therefore this Court is of the view that PW15 Tika Ram is not a competent witness to depose on alleged violation of any policy or rule by accused DDA officials as he is not aware of the State vs Jai Parkash Ors on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199295568/

PW 2 Bimal Kumar Jain stated in his examination in chief dated 20.03.2013 that he was posted as Branch Manager (Oriental Bank of Commerce) in Mahipalpur for the period during February,
1996 to October, 2002.

During that period, some cheques issued by the DDA were encashed through their branch and OP Arora was hall in charge of the bank and his nature of duty was to open new accounts, to supervise and to look after the entire functioning of the branch, including clearing cash in hand, credit account, etc. except sanctioning loans.
Thereafter OP Arora had deposited the cheques issued by DDA in different accounts i.e. in the name of AK Soni.

The said cheque was deposited in the account no. 14369 of Shashi Bhushan by OP Arora in his own handwriting by mentioning the name of Ashok Kumar Soni in the pay in slip and O P Arora got the cheque cleared in clearing.
However, the clerk concerned objected that name of account holder mentioned in the above said pay in slip is different than the name of account holder shown in ledger.
Then OP Arora credited the amount in the sundry account of the bank and from there, he transferred the funds without authority to debit the amount in the savings account no. 14369 of Shashi Bhushan.
PW2 further stated that OP Arora did not obtain any request letter from Shashi Bhushan to credit the amount lying in sundry account.
14. PW2 in his cross-examination dated 06.09.2013 stated that he cannot say whether the account Ex. PW2/B was opened by Shashi Bhushan or not.
15. On perusal of above testimony of PW2 this Court is of the view that there is no sufficient evidence on record to show that the said Bank account was opened by Shashi Bhushan.
Further it is evident from the testimony of PW2 that the withdrawal slip and the pay in slip pertaining to deposit of cheque of Rs.

16. Further there is no evidence on record to show that the cheque of Rs. 1,21,266/- was deposited in the bank on the instruction of accused DDA officials or accused Shashi Bhushan.
Further there is no evidence to show that the accused DDA officials were the beneficiary of the refund in the name of Abhishek Soni through cheque.
Further there is no evidence of any communication of accused DDA officials with accused OP Arora or Shashi Bhushan.
